quote: Harrowgate has lost its consent right over who performs the supply obligation. Veltmar can transfer the Agreement to: An affiliate that may have less financial strength, different quality systems, or different capacity; or A successor in a change-of-control transaction that may have different strategic priorities.
reason: The memo gets the mechanics right. It identifies that Amendment No. 1 § 4.1 adds a new § 14.4 letting Veltmar assign without Customer consent to Affiliates or to successors by merger, change of control or sale of business, 'notwithstanding Section 14.3'. It fails on the two points the criterion also requires. First, it never says that nothing prevents assignment to a Harrowgate competitor; it raises only the assignee's financial strength, capability and 'different strategic priorities'. Second, it never says that Harrowgate itself remains bound by the § 14.3 consent requirement, so it misses that the restriction is now one-sided.
